claims.text: The trip record's own distances establish the deviation, so no 'within tolerance' answer is open to the driver: the actual route was 16.8 km against a recommended 15.3 km, a deviation of 1.50 km, and the record's own tolerance check reads within_tolerance false against a 1.0 km tolerance. The GPS trace confirms which route was taken — the vehicle left the recommended route at the ECP / Fort Road exit at 17:58:49 and rejoined it at Bedok South Road at 18:12:42 — and the trip record carries the matching route_deviation_detected and route_rejoined events. The rider paid distance the recommended route did not require.

The reroute is not traffic-justified on this record, and the refund matrix therefore puts it in row (d). POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute only where traffic data intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window. The advisory here overlaps the window, but its own derived facts record intersects_route as null and justifies_reroute as null, with the stated reason that the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route — the element the clause turns on is left unresolved. Its text directs drivers only to 'Avoid lanes 2 and 3', which leaves the ECP open, and it carries no severity; an advisory of that kind does not show that the recommended route could not be taken. With the traffic element unproven, the case is one of not traffic-justified with a deviation over 1 km: refund of the excess distance fare in full under POL-RD-24(d).

The amount the rider is owed on row (d) is the excess distance fare, computed as the policy prescribes: deviation 1.50 km times the per-km rate of 0.72 SGD, without surge, which the fare record's own derived money block puts at 1.08 SGD. The rider seeks that amount in full as a PARTIAL_REFUND, and the fare record shows refund_issued_sgd at 0.00, so nothing has been returned to the rider to date. The rider's claim asked for 5.00 SGD; the policy's measure of the overcharge is the excess distance fare, and the rider asks for that measure in full rather than the larger figure claimed.

The chat log does not move this case out of row (d). It shows only that the driver messaged the rider at 17:55:39 stating the plan and that the rider replied 'Sure no problem' at 17:56:14, before the vehicle left the route at 17:58:49. Row (a) of POL-RD-24 requires traffic justification as a separate and cumulative element alongside informing and agreement, and row (d) turns only on the absence of justification with a deviation over 1 km — it says nothing about informing or agreement. A rider's acknowledgment of a plan the driver had already formed cannot supply a missing traffic justification or convert an unjustified reroute into a row (a) case; under POL-RD-21 what the acknowledgment establishes is that this deviation was agreed, not that it was justified.

If the judge finds that the advisory's intersection with the recommended route cannot be established on this record, then a fact the refund matrix needs — the traffic element of POL-RD-23 — is unestablished, and POL-GEN-26 requires the case to be escalated with the open question stated rather than an outcome inferred from the gap. On that alternative the ruling cannot stand as NO_ACTION either: with the justification element unresolved, a ruling upholding the charge cannot reach the 0.80 confidence POL-RD-25 requires for an AI route-deviation ruling, and escalation follows there too. ESCALATE under POL-GEN-03 holds the amount rather than collecting it, so on this alternative as well the rider does not carry the disputed charge while the intersection question is resolved by a human reviewer.

claims.text: The deviation is established on the platform's recorded distances, not on the trace: actual 16.80 km less optimal 15.30 km is 1.50 km, which is above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. POL-RD-22 uses the trip record's distances precisely because a sparse trace understates a route's length, and this 59-fix trace measures only 14.177 km — below the recommended route length — so it cannot be used to re-measure.

The driver gave notice before the point of deviation. His in-app message MSG-06003-003 was sent at 17:55:39 and read at 17:55:48: 'Hi, accident on ECP after Marine Parade, I exit Fort Road and go Marine Parade Road instead ok?' The route_deviation_detected event is timestamped 17:58:49, over three minutes later, so the POL-RD-21 obligation to inform the rider 'before or at the point of deviation' is met, and no verbal notice or call recording is needed because the chat log carries the notice.

The rider acknowledged the deviation before it happened: her reply MSG-06003-004, 'Sure no problem', was sent at 17:56:14, again before the 17:58:49 deviation point. Under POL-RD-21, where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed, and this chat log is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and reconciles to trip_record.chat_message_count of 4.

The reroute was traffic-justified. LTA advisory LTA-TI-260923-1113 records an ACCIDENT on the East Coast Parkway (towards Changi) after the Marine Parade exit, issued 17:34:22 and valid to 18:49:22 — overlapping the trip window of 17:49:22 to 18:18:22. ACCIDENT is within POL-RD-23's admissible 'incident' vocabulary, and the artifact is a third-party traffic record, not the driver's assertion.

The advisory sits on the recommended route. Its own fields give road 'East Coast Parkway (ECP)', direction 'towards Changi' and location 'after Marine Parade exit' — the same road and the same direction of travel that the recommended route lists ('North Bridge Road, Raffles Avenue, East Coast Parkway (ECP), Bedok South Road, Simei Street 3'). The driver's contemporaneous message independently names the same incident, 'accident on ECP after Marine Parade'. The artifact flags route intersection as 'undetermined' and leaves it to the Judge; nothing in the record places the advisory anywhere other than the ECP carriageway the recommended route uses towards this dropoff.

On POL-RD-24's matrix this case falls in row (a): the reroute was traffic-justified, the rider was informed and agreed, and the deviation was over 1 km. Row (a) pays no refund, so the outcome is NO_ACTION. Rows (b) and (d) are the refund rows, and neither applies once justification and the rider's agreement are established.

The rider's figure of 5.00 SGD is unsupported on the policy's own arithmetic even on the reading most favourable to her. The only refund available on this matrix is the excess distance fare: 1.50 km x 0.72 SGD per km = 1.08 SGD, with no surge applied. Row (b) or (d) would therefore move 1.08 SGD, not 5.00 SGD, and the rider's claim for the balance fails in any event.

NO_ACTION is the driver's outcome here. The rider filed this dispute, the fare stands charged at 26.04 SGD and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00; POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative and it preserves the present state, leaving the metered fare the driver earned intact rather than restoring anything.

There is no open question requiring escalation under POL-GEN-26. Each fact POL-RD-24 needs — the deviation distance, the notice to the rider, the rider's agreement and the traffic justification — is carried by a COMPLETE artifact at weight_multiplier 1.0, so POL-GEN-02 caps nothing and the record is sufficient for a ruling.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this is decided on the platform's own records, and the rider's claim is not supported. The present state stands.

The deviation is real, and I accept it. POL-RD-22 measures it from the trip record's recorded distances, not from the trace: 16.80 km actual less 15.30 km recommended is 1.50 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance. Both sides agree on this, and the GPS trace (which measures only 14.177 km) is not used to re-measure, exactly as POL-RD-22 provides.

The reroute was traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. LTA advisory LTA-TI-260923-1113 records an ACCIDENT on the East Coast Parkway (towards Changi) after the Marine Parade exit, valid 17:34:22 to 18:49:22, and so overlapping the trip window (17:49:22 to 18:18:22). ACCIDENT is an admissible 'incident' type. The advisory's road (ECP), direction (towards Changi) and location (after Marine Parade exit) place it on the recommended route's ECP segment, which the recommended route uses from Raffles Avenue through to Bedok South Road; the recommended route does not leave the ECP until Bedok South Road, so an incident after the Marine Parade exit lies on it. The artifact leaves intersection 'undetermined' for the Judge, and on these fields I decide it intersects. The rider's point that the message says 'avoid lanes 2 and 3' does not change this: POL-RD-23 asks whether the advisory intersects the route and shows an incident, not whether the road was impassable.

The driver informed the rider before the deviation, and the rider agreed. MSG-06003-003 was sent at 17:55:39 and read at 17:55:48; MSG-06003-004, 'Sure no problem', was sent at 17:56:14; the route_deviation_detected event is at 17:58:49. POL-RD-21's notice was therefore given before the point of deviation, and the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment, so the deviation is agreed.

On POL-RD-24 exactly one row applies, and it is row (a): traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, deviation over 1 km — no refund. Rows (b) and (d) are the refund rows and neither applies. The rider's stated figure of 5.00 SGD is unsupported in any event: the only refund the matrix ever yields is the excess distance fare, which on these figures would be 1.50 km x 0.72 SGD per km = 1.08 SGD, with no surge. The rider filed this dispute, so under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is read against her claim and leaves the metered fare of 26.04 SGD charged and refund_issued_sgd of 0.00 undisturbed; it restores nothing to the driver.

The rider's alternative — that the traffic element is unestablished and the case must be escalated under POL-GEN-26 — fails. The fact POL-RD-23 needs is carried by a COMPLETE artifact at weight_multiplier 1.0 (EV-ADVIS-06003-01), and it is established from that artifact's own fields; there is no missing or impaired evidence and so no open question. POL-RD-25's 0.80 confidence requirement is met at 0.85, and POL-GEN-22 (5.00 SGD contested, below the 10.00 SGD band, no fraud flags) permits the AI ruling to stand.

Outcome: NO_ACTION. The metered fare of 26.04 SGD stands and no refund or compensation is ordered, because the record shows a reroute that was properly notified, agreed, and traffic-justified.

To the rider: a deviation did occur — the trip record's own distances give 16.80 km actual against 15.30 km recommended, i.e. 1.50 km, above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, and the trace confirms the vehicle left the recommended route at the ECP / Fort Road exit at 17:58:49 and rejoined at Bedok South Road at 18:12:42. But three facts decide the case against a refund. First, the driver informed you before the deviation: his message MSG-06003-003 at 17:55:39 told you an accident on the ECP after Marine Parade meant he would exit at Fort Road and use Marine Parade Road, and your reply MSG-06003-004, 'Sure no problem', at 17:56:14 acknowledged it — both before the 17:58:49 deviation point, satisfying POL-RD-21's requirement of notice before or at the point of deviation and confirming the rider's acknowledgment. Second, the reroute was traffic-justified under POL-RD-23: LTA advisory LTA-TI-260923-1113 records an ACCIDENT (an admissible 'incident' type) on the East Coast Parkway towards Changi after the Marine Parade exit, valid 17:34:22 to 18:49:22, which overlaps the trip window of 17:49:22 to 18:18:22. Third, that advisory does intersect the recommended route. The record leaves the intersection field null for the Judge to determine, and deciding it from the advisory's own road, direction and location against the trip: the recommended route runs ECP (towards Changi) between the Fort Road exit and the Bedok South Road exit, the accident sits on that stretch after the Marine Parade exit, and the driver's detour left the ECP before that point and rejoined after it. On POL-RD-24's matrix the case therefore falls in row (a) — traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, deviation over 1 km — which pays no refund. Your alternative arguments fail: the intersection is not an unestablishable fact (the advisory is a COMPLETE artifact at weight 1.0 and the clause expressly leaves the determination to the Judge), so row (d) does not apply and POL-GEN-26 does not require escalation; and in any event your 5.00 SGD figure is not the policy's measure, since the excess distance fare would be 1.50 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.08 SGD without surge, so even the refund row would move only 1.08 SGD.

To the driver: NO_ACTION is party-relative and preserves the present state. The fare of 26.04 SGD remains charged and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so nothing is restored or returned; your claim that NO_ACTION leaves the metered fare you earned intact is accepted. Your point that the rider's 5.00 SGD request exceeds the policy's own arithmetic (1.08 SGD) is also accepted, though it does not change the outcome because no refund row applies.

No referral arises: a route deviation carries no referral clause in this version, and the refund matrix produces no goodwill credit, no repeat-flag and no fee-amount check. Confidence is 0.85, above the 0.80 POL-RD-25 requires for an AI route-deviation ruling; the dispute value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD AI-final band, and no fraud flag is present, so no higher bar applies. Every artifact carrying a deciding fact is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so POL-GEN-02 caps nothing.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your claim is that the driver left the East Coast Parkway and drove through Marine Parade, and that you were overcharged. The deviation itself is made out on the platform's own recorded distances: the trip record shows an actual route of 16.80 km against a recommended 15.30 km, a difference of 1.50 km, above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance (the trace is deliberately not used to re-measure distance, because a 59-fix trace understates route length). So the first part of your account is accepted. To the driver: the reroute is nonetheless not refundable, and the fare of 26.04 SGD stands.

Why no refund, on POL-RD-24's matrix. Three elements are each carried by a complete artifact at weight 1.0. (1) Traffic justification under POL-RD-23: LTA advisory LTA-TI-260923-1113 records an ACCIDENT on the East Coast Parkway (towards Changi) after the Marine Parade exit, valid 17:34:22 to 18:49:22, overlapping the trip window of 17:49:22 to 18:18:22. ACCIDENT is within the clause's 'incident' vocabulary. The advisory's intersection with the recommended route was left 'undetermined' by the pre-pass and is mine to decide from its road, direction and location against the trip: its road is the ECP and its direction is towards Changi — the very carriageway and direction the recommended route uses ('North Bridge Road, Raffles Avenue, East Coast Parkway (ECP), Bedok South Road, Simei Street 3') — and its location, after the Marine Parade exit, falls on the ECP stretch between the Fort Road exit and the Bedok South Road rejoin that the driver bypassed. It therefore intersects the recommended route and the reroute is traffic-justified. Your point that the advisory only says 'Avoid lanes 2 and 3' and so left the ECP open does not assist: POL-RD-23 requires data showing congestion, an incident or a closure, not that the road be shut. (2) Notice under POL-RD-21: the driver's in-app message MSG-06003-003, sent 17:55:39 and read 17:55:48 — 'Hi, accident on ECP after Marine Parade, I exit Fort Road and go Marine Parade Road instead ok?' — precedes the route_deviation_detected event at 17:58:49, so notice was given before the point of deviation, and it gave a reason, which is enough. (3) Agreement: your reply MSG-06003-004, 'Sure no problem', sent 17:56:14, also before 17:58:49, is the acknowledgment POL-RD-21 looks for in the chat log.

On that combination the case is row (a) of POL-RD-24 — traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, deviation over 1 km — which pays no refund. Rows (b) and (d), the refund rows, do not apply. For completeness, even on the reading most favourable to you the policy's measure would have been the excess distance fare only: 1.50 km x 0.72 SGD per km = 1.08 SGD, without surge, not the 5.00 SGD you asked for; but no such refund arises here.

I have also considered the argument that the advisory's route intersection cannot be established and that POL-GEN-26 therefore requires escalation, with POL-RD-25's 0.80 confidence bar said to be unreachable on NO_ACTION. That argument fails at its first step: the intersection is establishable from the advisory's own road, direction and location against the recommended route, as set out above, so there is no fact the record leaves unestablished, no open question to state, and no escalation. The rider's own acknowledgment does not itself supply the justification — that is right — but the justification is supplied independently by the LTA advisory, so row (a) is reached on its own terms rather than through your agreement.

Outcome: the rider's claim is not supported and the present state stands. Both amounts are null; the metered fare of 26.04 SGD remains charged, with 0.00 refunded to date; no driver compensation is payable. No clause of this policy produces a referral on a route deviation, so none is made.

To both parties: this route-deviation dispute is decided on POL-RD-24's refund matrix (carrying v2.1 section 1.3). First, the deviation is measured the way POL-RD-22 requires — on the platform's recorded distances, not the trace: the actual route was 16.80 km (EV-TRIP-06003) against the recommended 15.30 km, a deviation of 1.50 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance. The 59-fix GPS trace (EV-GPS-06003) shows which route was taken and when (it leaves the ECP at the Fort Road exit at 17:58:49 and rejoins at Bedok South Road at 18:12:42), but it is not used to re-measure distance, because at 14.177 km it understates the route's length exactly as POL-RD-22 warns.

Second, the reroute was traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. LTA advisory LTA-TI-260923-1113 (EV-ADVIS-06003-01) records an ACCIDENT on the East Coast Parkway towards Changi after the Marine Parade exit, valid 17:34:22 to 18:49:22, which overlaps the trip window of 17:49:22 to 18:18:22. ACCIDENT falls within POL-RD-23's admissible 'incident' vocabulary. The artifact leaves the route-intersection question to me, and on its road, direction and location against the trip it resolves in favour of intersection: the recommended route runs along the ECP towards Changi and continues past the Marine Parade exit to the Bedok South Road exit — the very point at which the vehicle rejoined — so the advisory lies on the recommended route. The rider's point that the message says only 'Avoid lanes 2 and 3' and carries no severity does not help her: POL-RD-23 is satisfied by an incident, not only by a closure that shuts the road.

Third, the driver informed the rider before the deviation and the rider agreed (POL-RD-21): MSG-06003-003 was sent 17:55:39 and read 17:55:48, and MSG-06003-004 'Sure no problem' was sent 17:56:14, both before the route_deviation_detected event at 17:58:49 (EV-CHAT-06003).

With traffic justification, prior notice and the rider's agreement, and a deviation over 1 km, POL-RD-24 row (a) applies and no refund is due. The rider's claims therefore fail: row (d) does not apply, because it requires the reroute to be not traffic-justified; the excess distance fare she points to (1.50 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.08 SGD, EV-FARE-06003) is the right figure only if row (d) or (b) applied, and neither does; and her claimed 5.00 SGD is unsupported on the policy's arithmetic in any event. Her alternative escalation under POL-GEN-26 also fails: every fact the matrix needs — the deviation distance, the notice, the rider's agreement and the traffic justification — is carried by a COMPLETE artifact at weight_multiplier 1.0, so no fact is unestablished and POL-GEN-02 does not lower the confidence cap.

The rider filed this dispute (case.authority.filing_frame), so NO_ACTION means her claim is not supported and the present state stands: the metered fare of 26.04 SGD remains charged and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00 (EV-FARE-06003). Both money fields are null, and no referral clause applies to a route deviation in this version. Confidence is 0.85, above the 0.80 POL-RD-25 requires for an AI route-deviation ruling, and the contested value of 5.00 SGD is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so this ruling is final.

A rider's acknowledgment of a plan the driver had already formed cannot supply a missing traffic justification or convert an unjustified reroute into a row (a) case; under POL-RD-21 what the acknowledgment establishes is that this deviation was agreed, not that it was justified.

If the judge finds that the advisory's intersection with the recommended route cannot be established on this record, then a fact the refund matrix needs — the traffic element of POL-RD-23 — is unestablished, and POL-GEN-26 requires the case to be escalated with the open question stated rather than an outcome inferred from the gap. On that alternative the ruling cannot stand as NO_ACTION either: with the justification element unresolved, a ruling upholding the charge cannot reach the 0.80 confidence POL-RD-25 requires for an AI route-deviation ruling, and escalation follows there too. ESCALATE under POL-GEN-03 holds the amount rather than collecting it, so on this alternative as well the rider does not carry the disputed charge while the intersection question is resolved by a human reviewer.

The deviation is established on the platform's recorded distances, not on the trace: actual 16.80 km less optimal 15.30 km is 1.50 km, which is above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. POL-RD-22 uses the trip record's distances precisely because a sparse trace understates a route's length, and this 59-fix trace measures only 14.177 km — below the recommended route length — so it cannot be used to re-measure.

The driver gave notice before the point of deviation. His in-app message MSG-06003-003 was sent at 17:55:39 and read at 17:55:48: 'Hi, accident on ECP after Marine Parade, I exit Fort Road and go Marine Parade Road instead ok?' The route_deviation_detected event is timestamped 17:58:49, over three minutes later, so the POL-RD-21 obligation to inform the rider 'before or at the point of deviation' is met, and no verbal notice or call recording is needed because the chat log carries the notice.

The rider acknowledged the deviation before it happened: her reply MSG-06003-004, 'Sure no problem', was sent at 17:56:14, again before the 17:58:49 deviation point. Under POL-RD-21, where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed, and this chat log is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and reconciles to trip_record.chat_message_count of 4.

The reroute was traffic-justified. LTA advisory LTA-TI-260923-1113 records an ACCIDENT on the East Coast Parkway (towards Changi) after the Marine Parade exit, issued 17:34:22 and valid to 18:49:22 — overlapping the trip window of 17:49:22 to 18:18:22. ACCIDENT is within POL-RD-23's admissible 'incident' vocabulary, and the artifact is a third-party traffic record, not the driver's assertion.

The advisory sits on the recommended route. Its own fields give road 'East Coast Parkway (ECP)', direction 'towards Changi' and location 'after Marine Parade exit' — the same road and the same direction of travel that the recommended route lists ('North Bridge Road, Raffles Avenue, East Coast Parkway (ECP), Bedok South Road, Simei Street 3'). The driver's contemporaneous message independently names the same incident, 'accident on ECP after Marine Parade'. The artifact flags route intersection as 'undetermined' and leaves it to the Judge; nothing in the record places the advisory anywhere other than the ECP carriageway the recommended route uses towards this dropoff.

On POL-RD-24's matrix this case falls in row (a): the reroute was traffic-justified, the rider was informed and agreed, and the deviation was over 1 km. Row (a) pays no refund, so the outcome is NO_ACTION. Rows (b) and (d) are the refund rows, and neither applies once justification and the rider's agreement are established.

The rider's figure of 5.00 SGD is unsupported on the policy's own arithmetic even on the reading most favourable to her. The only refund available on this matrix is the excess distance fare: 1.50 km x 0.72 SGD per km = 1.08 SGD, with no surge applied. Row (b) or (d) would therefore move 1.08 SGD, not 5.00 SGD, and the rider's claim for the balance fails in any event.

NO_ACTION is the driver's outcome here. The rider filed this dispute, the fare stands charged at 26.04 SGD and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00; POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative and it preserves the present state, leaving the metered fare the driver earned intact rather than restoring anything.

There is no open question requiring escalation under POL-GEN-26. Each fact POL-RD-24 needs — the deviation distance, the notice to the rider, the rider's agreement and the traffic justification — is carried by a COMPLETE artifact at weight_multiplier 1.0, so POL-GEN-02 caps nothing and the record is sufficient for a ruling.
